title: Performance Optimization Applied Check
description: Practice diagnosing render cost, memoization pitfalls, code splitting tradeoffs, virtualization, and profiler-driven optimization.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A memoized child still re-renders because the parent passes onSave={() => save(id)} every render. What can help if the child is expensive?

options.text: useCallback with correct dependencies or redesigning the prop
Removing all props
Calling setState in render
Wrapping the child in BrowserRouter

questions.explanation: React.memo uses shallow comparison, so unstable function props can cause re-renders.

questions.prompt: When is React.memo most likely to help? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The component renders often with the same props
Rendering the component is meaningfully expensive
Props are stable or can be made stable
The component always reads a rapidly changing context

questions.explanation: Memoization helps when repeated renders can be skipped and comparison is cheaper than rendering.

questions.prompt: A useMemo result is stale because a variable used inside is missing from dependencies. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Add the missing dependency or restructure the calculation
Disable dependencies permanently
Move the variable to a comment
Use React.memo on the parent only

questions.explanation: Memoized values must list all reactive inputs they read.

questions.prompt: Memoizing everything can make code harder to maintain and may add overhead without improving user experience.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Memoization has cost and complexity, so it should follow measured need.

questions.prompt: A page imports a heavy chart only used after opening an analytics route. What optimization fits?

options.text: Route-level or component-level lazy loading with a good fallback
Rendering the chart hidden on every page
Putting the chart data in context
Replacing all state with refs

questions.explanation: Lazy loading defers expensive code until users need that UI.

questions.prompt: What should you watch when virtualizing a list? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Row height assumptions
Overscan amount
Keyboard and screen reader accessibility
Removing all item keys

questions.explanation: Virtualized lists need careful sizing, buffering, and accessibility behavior.

questions.prompt: The profiler shows a slow parent recalculating an expensive filtered list every render. What is a likely fix?

options.text: Move unnecessary state down and memoize the expensive calculation with correct dependencies
Add an empty dependency effect to set the same state
Use document.querySelector
Remove all dependency arrays

questions.explanation: State placement and useMemo can reduce repeated expensive work when inputs are unchanged.

questions.prompt: Why measure before and after an optimization?

options.text: To verify the change improved the real bottleneck
To make React.memo required everywhere
To avoid writing JSX
To convert browser state to server state

questions.explanation: Profiling confirms that optimization work targets and improves the actual issue.
